en: A Hymn of Victory over Māra: Praise to the Sole Teacher of the World, who has conquered the Kali age of Māra, and who is bowed to by gods, yakṣas, mahoragas, and daityas.
I always pay homage to this Guṇamegha, who has well taught the path of the Four Noble Truths. || 1 ||
Having beheld people caught in the midst of the terrifying great ocean of existence and crying out in piteous distress,
he who has made here the vow to liberate them—
I bow down to that All-pervading Lord whom he brought forth. || 2 ||
Resembling the king of mountains, with the splendor of the autumnal moon, fair-faced, with beautiful arms, and possessing excellent form—
homage to the Sugata, the peerless one who has attained the state of the Sugata.
I am forever prostrate before the one who acts for the welfare of the world. || 3 ||
His body was completely suffused with a golden radiance,
and he moved with the slow, steady gait of an elephant or a swan, as majestic as a great rain-cloud or a noble drum.
I bow my head in reverence to the sole treasure-house of virtues.
With eyes like the rising sun,
with the terrifying roar of flashing and fierce great thunderbolts,
and bearing swords and spears like the slayers of Namuci—
O All-pervading Lord, you have indeed not been moved by these distortions.
With earlobes as pale as the *lavalī* fruit,
their vine-like bodies bent under the weight of their breasts,
the daughters of the *nāgas* were indeed unable to endure you.
Even by sighs and faltering steps, one might cause her to tremble.
Trees adorned with clusters of blossoms and mountains variegated with thousands of precious gems do not produce such delight for the virtuous as [the sight of] those who have attained liberation.
Just as they produce your heroic qualities. || 7 ||

Beholding your speech— which possesses clear and variegated words, is endowed with many logical arguments, is intelligible, is pleasant to the ear, and bears the fruit of the auspicious path— people [are inspired].
They do not utter any other words again except for yours.
Thus, having beheld this refuge of yours, people do not fall into hell even for hundreds of eons,
having utterly destroyed their many enemies in the form of the afflictions.
They proceed toward the excellent city of liberation, which is pure. || 9 ||
Even the moon, its darkness overcome by your gentleness, does not shine in the sky because of your splendor,
which possesses the luster of gold and saffron.
Overwhelmed by her radiance, the sun does not shine. || 10 ||
O Lord, the bees that are the eyes of men fall upon your auspicious lotus-face,
which is like a stainless lotus with blossomed petals.
Like bees agitated by hundreds of flowers. || 11 ||
Thus, having proclaimed even these mere fragments of your names with incomparable and excellent *toṭaka* mantras,
whatever abundant merit has been acquired by me today—
May there be auspiciousness for gods and men upon the earth because of that. || 12 ||
The Śrīmāravijayastotra is completed.
